mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns in triggered months are not statistically higher than in untriggered months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising labor market tightness, measured by PAYEMS, coincides with stronger S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as firms anticipate higher wage growth and invest accordingly.
failure_condition: In regimes with rising unemployment (UNRATE < 4%), the 60-day forward return correlation with PAYEMS change is negative and statistically significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO falling by ≥2% month-over-month) predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days as market anticipates soft demand and potential production cuts.
failure_condition: Over 20 consecutive contraction months, the 5-day forward return is never negative when INDPRO declines by ≥2% (empirical probability > 0.95).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in retail sales (HOUST) above trend for two consecutive months signals resilient consumer demand, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST month-over-month increase for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During periods of high unemployment (>8%), HOUST two-month up moves fail to predict positive 20-day forward returns (correlation < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains above 4% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 exhibits negative forward returns over the next 20 days as investors anticipate higher borrowing costs and muted growth.
failure_condition: In regimes with falling inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2%), the negative return prediction fails to materialize (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE falling by ≥0.2 percentage points) combined with rising wage growth (PAYEMS) creates a labor market surprise that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE month-over-month decline ≥ 0.2% AND PAYEMS month-over-month increase ≥ 1%
failure_condition: Across 100 such triggered months, the 60-day forward return is never in the top quartile compared to untriggered months (quantile rank < 25%).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive declines in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer confidence (not available in evidence catalog; fallback: use HOUST decline) over two months signal a dual softening that predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month decline ≥ 2% AND HOUST month-over-month decline ≥ 3% in the same month
failure_condition: In regimes with simultaneous GDP growth > 2%, the 5-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in RSAFS (money supply growth) above 6% in a non-inflationary regime predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as markets anticipate future asset price expansion.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS month-over-month increase ≥ 6% AND CPIAUCSL month-over-month increase < 0.2%
failure_condition: During high-inflation periods (CPIAUCSL > 3%), the positive return prediction fails (empirical probability < 0.2).
